# Documentation Authority Index

This index classifies every document under `docs/` and `.claude/semantic-model/`
into an authority class, so a reader (human or agent) knows how much weight to
give a claim before acting on it. `just lint-docs` (AC-004) machine-checks the
`authority` frontmatter field against the closed set of values below for each
glob it scans.

## Document classes

| Slug | Covers | Glob(s) checked by `lint-docs` |
|---|---|---|
| `normative` | `docs/01-spec.md` and accepted `.claude/specs/*` spec@1 acceptance criteria -- authoritative for current required behavior | `docs/*.md` |
| `rationale` | `docs/00-design.md` -- explains why, not a second source of current requirements | `docs/*.md` |
| `reference` | `docs/03-polyglot-spec.md`, `docs/04-python-engine-spec.md`, `docs/05-go-engine-spec.md` -- subsystem/engine design references | `docs/*.md` |
| `guide` | `docs/06-publishing.md`, `docs/release-paradigms.md`, and `docs/AUTHORITY.md` itself -- operational how-to material; `AUTHORITY.md` is classified `guide` because it explains how to classify and maintain documentation rather than asserting product behavior | `docs/*.md` |
| `historical-context` | `docs/01-research-brief.md`, `docs/02-library-vs-moon-decision.md`, and handoff documents such as `.claude/plans/SESSION_HANDOFF.md` -- a record of past research or decisions, not current truth | `docs/*.md` (handoffs under `.claude/plans/` are not scanned; see `plan-status` below) |
| `verified-current` | `.claude/semantic-model/*.md` -- describes the implementation as verified against the current codebase | `.claude/semantic-model/*.md` |
| `plan-status` | `.claude/plans/*.md` -- intended work and per-track status | Not scanned by `lint-docs` (AC-005) |
| `spec-metadata` | A convention, not a frontmatter slug, applying only to files listed in `.claude/specs/.authority-enrolled` (AC-002) | Not part of the `docs/*.md` or `.claude/semantic-model/*.md` frontmatter check; checked separately by `lint-docs` Scan 2 |

## Conflict resolution

The normative source (`docs/01-spec.md` or an accepted spec) always wins. When
a non-normative document is found to conflict with it, the non-normative
document receives a dated correction note in place, pointing to the normative
source -- never a silent rewrite of its own original claims.

## `.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md` heading convention (prose policy, not enforced)

A `.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md` section heading marking a track `DONE`,
`SUPERSEDED`, or `CLOSED` should reference the SPEC-id, REQ-id, or file path
it implements in its body text. This is guidance for authors, not a
criterion any check in this repository verifies -- `.claude/plans/` is never
scanned by `lint-docs` (AC-005).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""just lint-docs: documentation authority check (SPEC-DOCUMENTATION-AUTHORITY-005).

Scan 1 (frontmatter authority): every docs/*.md and .claude/semantic-model/*.md
file must carry a YAML frontmatter block with an `authority` key, valid for
its glob's closed set (docs/AUTHORITY.md).

Scan 2 (spec metadata): every filename listed in
.claude/specs/.authority-enrolled must name a .claude/specs/<filename> JSON
file carrying non-empty status, last_verified_revision, and owner_track
top-level fields, with status one of draft, proposed, accepted, superseded.

Exits 0 and prints one summary line on success. Exits 1 and prints one
labeled violation per line on failure. Never rewrites any file. Does not
scan .claude/plans/ at all (AC-005).
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

DOCS_VALID = {"normative", "rationale", "reference", "guide", "historical-context"}
SEMANTIC_MODEL_VALID = {"verified-current"}
SPEC_STATUS_VALID = {"draft", "proposed", "accepted", "superseded"}


def extract_frontmatter(text):
    """Return (frontmatter_dict_or_None, malformed).

    malformed is True only when the file opens with a '---' line (a
    frontmatter block was attempted) but the block has no closing '---',
    or its content does not parse as a YAML mapping.
    """
    lines = text.splitlines()
    if not lines or lines[0].strip() != "---":
        return None, False
    try:
        end = lines.index("---", 1)
    except ValueError:
        return None, True
    block = "\n".join(lines[1:end])
    try:
        data = yaml.safe_load(block)
    except yaml.YAMLError:
        return None, True
    if data is not None and not isinstance(data, dict):
        return None, True
    return (data or {}), False


def scan1(root: Path):
    violations = []
    checked = 0
    groups = [
        (root / "docs", "*.md", DOCS_VALID),
        (root / ".claude" / "semantic-model", "*.md", SEMANTIC_MODEL_VALID),
    ]
    for directory, pattern, valid_set in groups:
        for path in sorted(directory.glob(pattern)):
            checked += 1
            rel = path.relative_to(root)
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            fm, malformed = extract_frontmatter(text)
            if malformed:
                violations.append(f"{rel}: malformed frontmatter")
                continue
            if fm is None or "authority" not in fm:
                violations.append(f"{rel}: missing authority field")
                continue
            value = fm["authority"]
            if value not in valid_set:
                violations.append(f"{rel}: invalid authority value: {value}")
    return checked, violations


def scan2(root: Path):
    violations = []
    checked = 0
    enrollment_file = root / ".claude" / "specs" / ".authority-enrolled"
    if not enrollment_file.exists():
        return checked, violations
    for line in enrollment_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        filename = line.strip()
        if not filename:
            continue
        checked += 1
        spec_path = root / ".claude" / "specs" / filename
        rel = Path(".claude/specs") / filename
        if not spec_path.exists():
            violations.append(f"{rel}: missing spec-metadata field: status")
            continue
        try:
            data = json.loads(spec_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            violations.append(f"{rel}: missing spec-metadata field: status")
            continue
        for field in ("status", "last_verified_revision", "owner_track"):
            if not data.get(field):
                violations.append(f"{rel}: missing spec-metadata field: {field}")
        status = data.get("status")
        if status and status not in SPEC_STATUS_VALID:
            violations.append(f"{rel}: invalid spec-metadata status: {status}")
    return checked, violations


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Documentation authority check.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--root",
        default=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent),
        help="Repository root to scan (default: this script's repo root).",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    root = Path(args.root).resolve()

    c1, v1 = scan1(root)
    c2, v2 = scan2(root)
    violations = v1 + v2
    total = c1 + c2

    if violations:
        for v in violations:
            print(v)
        return 1
    print(f"lint-docs: {total} files checked, 0 violations")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

No task touches Rust code or crate compilation boundaries -- batches are grouped by logical concern (authority docs, spec metadata, frontmatter, tooling) rather than a Cargo compilation unit, mirroring PLAN-006's batch-docs precedent for text-only work.
